threads.Author: codex
threads.Text: [Q] Scope decision: this makes the first proof agent-readable and terminal-readable, not yet glanceable in the existing human review UI. Is that sufficient for the dogfood before we invest in a rail?
threads.SectionPath: Lightweight Plan Ledger > What We're NOT Doing

Anchor.selected_text: - No TUI or browser progress UI in the first dogfood; `context` establishes the read contract.
Anchor.context_before: - No checkpoint or progress write command and no execution state in the sidecar; agents edit Markdown directly.
Anchor.context_after: - No semantic judgment that evidence proves a claim; progress reports recorded state and references.

threads.Text: [Q] This is the core lightweight-state choice: an append-only phase ledger rather than editable tasks. Corrections become new checkpoints, which preserves auditability but may add noise. Confirm this tradeoff.
threads.SectionPath: Lightweight Plan Ledger > Implementation Phases > Phase 1 — define status as a plan-template convention

Anchor.selected_text: Each dated top-level entry names its state, then nests Summary, Evidence, and Next bullets; latest wins.
Anchor.context_before: Parse H3 phases beneath `Implementation Phases` and optional H4 `Status` sections.
Anchor.context_after: Guide every new phase toward this shape through the plan template and maintained example.

threads.SectionPath: Lightweight Plan Ledger > Implementation Phases > Phase 2 — preserve approval while detecting plan drift

Anchor.selected_text: Human approval covers phase definitions, success criteria, scope, and design—not progress updates.
Anchor.context_after: Record full document and plan-intent hashes on new signoffs.

Replies.Author: codex
Replies.Text: Clarified in the plan: approval covers stable intent—phase definitions, success criteria, scope, and design. Status-list edits do not invalidate it; changing that stable intent does, which prevents silent drift after human alignment.
